content: 1. Indinavir and Cannabidiol: Indinavir increases cannabidiol levels by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose and monitor closely for adverse effects. 2. Indinavir and Capivasertib: Indinavir raises capivasertib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or reduce the capivasertib dose if necessary, while monitoring for toxicity. 3. Indinavir and Capmatinib: Indinavir increases capmatinib levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Indinavir and Carbamazepine: Indinavir elevates carbamazepine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor plasma levels closely. Conversely, carbamazepine reduces indinavir levels, so alternative drugs should be considered. 5. Indinavir and Cariprazine: Indinavir increases cariprazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Reduce the cariprazine dose and monitor for side effects. 6. Indinavir and Cenobamate: Cenobamate decreases indinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4. Adjust the indinavir dose as needed and monitor closely. 7. Indinavir and Ceritinib: Indinavir increases ceritinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Indinavir and Chlordiazepoxide: Indinavir raises chlordiazepoxide levels, increasing the risk of toxicity. Consider alternative benzodiazepines or reduce the dose. 9. Indinavir and Ciclesonide (Inhaled): Indinavir increases ciclesonide levels, potentially causing Cushing's syndrome or adrenal suppression. Monitor closely for toxicity. 10. Indinavir and Cilostazol: Indinavir elevates cilostazol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Indinavir and Cimetidine: Cimetidine affects indinavir levels by altering gastric pH and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternatives. 12. Indinavir and Cinacalcet: Indinavir increases cinacalcet levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 13. Indinavir and Citalopram: Indinavir raises citalopram levels, increasing the risk of toxicity. Monitor closely. 14. Indinavir and Clarithromycin: Clarithromycin increases indinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor for toxicity. 15. Indinavir and Clomipramine: Indinavir elevates clomipramine levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely. 16. Indinavir and Clonazepam: Indinavir increases clonazepam levels, raising the risk of toxicity. Consider alternative benzodiazepines or reduce the dose. 17. Indinavir and Clopidogrel: Indinavir reduces clopidogrel activation by inhibiting CYP3A4. Monitor closely for reduced efficacy. 18. Indinavir and Clorazepate: Indinavir increases clorazepate levels, potentially causing toxicity. Consider alternatives or reduce the dose. 19. Indinavir and Clotrimazole: Clotrimazole decreases indinavir levels via P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Indinavir and Clozapine: Indinavir raises clozapine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 21. Indinavir and Cobicistat: Cobicistat significantly increases indinavir levels. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of severe toxicity. 22. Indinavir and Colchicine: Indinavir increases colchicine levels via P-gp and CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration, especially in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 23. Indinavir and Conivaptan: Conivaptan increases indinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. 24. Indinavir and Conjugated Estrogens: Indinavir elevates conjugated estrogen levels, increasing the risk of toxicity. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 25. Indinavir and Copanlisib: Indinavir raises copanlisib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or reduce the copanlisib dose. 26. Indinavir and Cortisone: Indinavir increases cortisone levels via CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibition. Monitor closely for toxicity. 27. Indinavir and Crizotinib: Indinavir elevates crizotinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Indinavir and Crofelemer: Crofelemer increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 in the gut. Monitor closely. 29. Indinavir and Cyclophosphamide: Indinavir raises cyclophosphamide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely. 30. Indinavir and Cyclosporine: Indinavir increases cyclosporine levels via CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibition. Monitor closely for toxicity. 31. Indinavir and Dabrafenib: Dabrafenib reduces indinavir levels, while indinavir increases dabrafenib levels. Avoid coadministration or use alternatives. 32. Indinavir and Danazol: Danazol increases indinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely. 33. Indinavir and Daridorexant: Indinavir raises daridorexant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternatives. 34. Indinavir and Darifenacin: Indinavir increases darifenacin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternatives. 35. Indinavir and Darolutamide: Indinavir raises darolutamide levels via CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibition. Monitor closely and adjust the darolutamide dose as needed. 36. Indinavir and Darunavir: Indinavir and darunavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitor closely. 37. Indinavir and Dasatinib: Indinavir elevates dasatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Indinavir and Deferasirox: Deferasirox reduces indinavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor closely. 39. Indinavir and Deflazacort: Indinavir increases deflazacort levels via CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibition. Reduce the deflazacort dose to one-third and monitor closely. 40. Indinavir and Desvenlafaxine: Indinavir raises desvenlafaxine levels, increasing the risk of toxicity. Monitor closely. 41. Indinavir and Dexamethasone: Indinavir elevates dexamethasone levels via CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Indinavir and Dexlansoprazole: Dexlansoprazole reduces indinavir levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid coadministration or use alternatives. 43. Indinavir and DHEA (Herbal): Indinavir increases DHEA levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely. 44. Indinavir and Diazepam: Indinavir raises diazepam levels, increasing the risk of toxicity. Consider alternatives or reduce the dose. 45. Indinavir and Diazoxide: Indinavir may cause hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Monitor closely. 46. Indinavir and Didanosine: Didanosine reduces indinavir levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer indinavir one hour before didanosine. 47. Indinavir and Dienogest/Estradiol Valerate: Indinavir alters estrogen and progestin levels, potentially causing adverse effects. Monitor closely. 48. Indinavir and Digoxin: Indinavir increases digoxin levels via P-gp inhibition. Monitor closely. 49. Indinavir and Dihydroergotamine: This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of severe toxicity. 50. Indinavir and Diltiazem: Indinavir raises diltiazem levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternatives. 51. Indinavir and Disopyramide: Indinavir increases disopyramide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely. 52. Indinavir and Docetaxel: Indinavir raises docetaxel levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely. 53. Indinavir and Dofetilide: Indinavir increases dofetilide levels, raising the risk of QT prolongation and arrhythmias. Use alternatives if possible. 54. Indinavir and Donepezil: Indinavir elevates donepezil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely. 55. Indinavir and Doravirine: Indinavir increases doravirine levels, potentially causing toxicity. Monitor closely. 56. Indinavir and Doxorubicin: Indinavir raises doxorubicin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely. 57. Indinavir and Dronabinol: Indinavir increases dronabinol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely. 58. Indinavir and Dronedarone: Indinavir raises dronedarone levels, increasing the risk of toxicity. Avoid coadministration or use alternatives. 59. Indinavir and Drospirenone: Indinavir increases drospirenone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely. 60. Indinavir and Dutasteride: Indinavir raises dutasteride levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely. This list highlights the importance of monitoring drug interactions involving indinavir, particularly due to its effects on the CYP3A4 enzyme and P-glycoprotein transporter.
